category_title: Students exhibiting aggressive behaviors and elopement during non-preferred academic tasks
minimal_context: Ann is sitting in the classroom and is asked to count objects on a math worksheet and then color them.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Ann, it is time for math. Please count the objects on this worksheet and then color them.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper and does not start counting, failing to comply with the instruction within 5 seconds.)

TUTOR: Come on, you need to finish your math assignment. Let's get started.

STUDENT: No! (Stands up, leaving contact with her designated chair for more than 3 seconds.)

TUTOR: Please sit back down in your chair and look at your worksheet.

STUDENT: (Throws the crayons at the tutor, rips the worksheet, and starts running out of the classroom without permission.)

options.A: Provide a preferred activity where she counts Lego blocks by colors as she constructs objects.
options.B: Bring in a mirror to help her see the reflection of her wrongly colored objects.
options.C: Let her work on the math worksheet without making any additional comments during the activity.
options.D: Stop her behavior and provide an explanation that not all the worksheet objects are counted.
